title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly improves large language model accuracy by grounding responses in retrieved passages. We explore agentic multi-hop reasoning and routing across heterogeneous vector indices.

title: Data Observability and Quality Gates for Production RAG Systems
summary: Silent data corruption in RAG pipelines degrades LLM answer faithfulness without throwing runtime errors. We introduce automated quality gates using Great Expectations 1.x to catch stale and malformed embeddings before serving.

title: Mitigating Ghost Vectors in Dense Retrieval via Idempotent Indexing
summary: Soft-deletions in vector databases leave orphaned embeddings that lead to hallucinations. This paper designs an idempotent index synchronization protocol that guarantees complete purges of outdated vector artifacts.

title: Freshness SLAs for Real-Time LLM Knowledge Augmentation
summary: We define freshness service-level agreements (SLAs) for temporal document ingestion. By tracking document age and update cadence, our orchestrator dynamically prioritizes recrawling high-churn technical corpora.

title: Evaluating Retrieval Precision with Token F1 and LLM Judges
summary: Evaluating open-domain QA requires robust metrics. We benchmark semantic similarity, token-level overlap F1, and model-based judge verdicts to quantify RAG answer correctness across noisy corpus conditions.

title: Semantic Layer Integration for Agentic Text-to-SQL Pipelines
summary: Connecting LLMs directly to raw warehouse tables often results in schema misunderstandings. A governed semantic layer standardizes business metric definitions, dramatically boosting SQL generation accuracy.

title: Synthetic Corruption Testing: Stress-Testing Vector Search Robustness
summary: We introduce an automated fuzzing suite that corrupts text chunks by injecting noise, truncating titles, and blanking summaries. Experiments reveal critical failure thresholds for dense embedding retrieval.

title: Multi-Agent Consensus for High-Stakes Fact Verification
summary: A single LLM is susceptible to confirmation bias when evaluating retrieved evidence. We demonstrate a multi-agent debate architecture where specialized verifier agents critique and corroborate citations.

title: Chunking Strategies for Technical Documentation Retrieval
summary: Hierarchical and semantic boundary chunking preserves code block contexts and markdown headings. Our benchmark demonstrates superior top-1 recall compared to fixed character length sliding windows.

title: Automated Data Quality Profiling with Great Expectations in CI/CD
summary: Embedding quality checks directly into data pipelines enables fail-closed governance. We show how Great Expectations suites catch schema drifts and null fields before documents reach the embedding model.

title: Hybrid Search Architectures: Combining BM25 with Dense Representations
summary: Dense vector search excels at conceptual similarity but struggles with exact acronyms and serial numbers. Reciprocal Rank Fusion of sparse lexical scores and dense embeddings achieves optimal recall.

title: Continuous Benchmark Evaluation for Enterprise Retrieval Pipelines
summary: Static benchmarks fail to capture domain drift in enterprise knowledge bases. We establish a synthetic test generator that auto-creates paired evaluation sets whenever new corpora are ingested.
